page: Microsoft Azure GS4-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor. The server is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 28.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 459 GB drive, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPUs included.

Performance benchmarks indicate a contrast between processing power and memory capacity. Single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor in the lower performance tiers, with a single-core Geekbench score of 621.0 and a multi-core score of 3433.0. However, memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is moderate at 454.13 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write speeds drop to 33.41 GB/sec and 13.09 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks show average performance, with Redis handling 6.85 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the GS4-8 trades raw CPU speed and modern instruction sets for massive memory capacity and local storage. It lacks AVX-512 capabilities, which limits its efficiency in advanced vector math, but supports standard AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and moderate database performance, this server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intense CPU throughput, such as caching layers, medium-sized database operations, and memory-bound legacy enterprise applications.
